title: FAIR Act ban on coordinator services and algorithmic rent setting
requirement: No rental property owner, agent, representative or subcontractor may exchange consideration for the services of a coordinator performing a coordinating function over residential dwelling units. The act takes effect the first day of the twelfth month after enactment.
coverage_conditions: All residential dwelling units in New Jersey, meaning any house, apartment, accessory unit or other unit intended for use as a primary residence, excluding medical, long-term care and detention facilities.
exemptions: Coordinating function excludes research or statistical analysis, published rent estimates made available to the public at no cost, listing databases offered on equal terms and government affordability controls; spreadsheets and query-only databases are not algorithmic devices.
penalty: A violation is a violation of the New Jersey Antitrust Act and does not limit the application of sections 6 through 17 of P.L.1970, c.73; the Attorney General must maintain a website location to receive complaints.
interaction: Construed in addition to the New Jersey Antitrust Act, which continues to apply to the same conduct.

title: Bar on municipal ordinances conflicting with the FAIR Act
requirement: A municipality may not enact any ordinance that conflicts with the FAIR Act, but this does not bar ordinances that another law explicitly authorizes or requires.
coverage_conditions: All municipalities in New Jersey and any rental property owner, coordinator or other person subject to the act.
exemptions: Ordinances explicitly authorized or required by any other law.
quoted_span:
b.    A municipality shall be prohibited from enacting
an ordinance that conflicts with this act.  This subsection shall not be
construed to prohibit the enactment of ordinances explicitly authorized or
required by any other law.
interaction: State act prevails over conflicting local ordinances on algorithmic rent setting.

title: San Diego just cause required for termination of tenancy
requirement: A landlord may not terminate a tenancy without just cause, meaning one of the at-fault grounds or one of the no-fault grounds listed in the Division, such as nonpayment, nuisance, owner occupancy or withdrawal from the rental market.
coverage_conditions: Tenancies of residential rental property in San Diego subject to Division 7, other than the property types listed in section 98.0703.

applicability.other: does not apply to housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years

exemptions: Hotels, short-term rentals, subsidized affordable housing other than Section 8, mobilehomes under the Mobilehome Residency Law, nonprofit and institutional housing, dormitories, rooms shared with a resident landlord, owner-occupied single-family homes and two-unit properties.
quoted_span:

interaction: Just cause termination must be consistent with California Civil Code section 1946.2; Division rights are in addition to state and federal rights.

title: Notice of residential tenant protections and statement of cause
requirement: A covered landlord must give the tenant written notice in no less than 12-point font with the required statements, including that local law requires a statement of cause in any notice to terminate a tenancy, and must provide the Tenant Protection Guide.
coverage_conditions: Residential rental property in San Diego that is subject to Division 7.
quoted_span:
written notice in no less than 12-point font to the tenant, and in a manner that
complies with California Civil Code section 1632, as may be amended, that
states as follows:
California law limits the amount your rent can be increased. See
California Civil Code section 1947.12 for more information. Local law
also provides that a landlord shall provide a statement of cause in any
notice to terminate a tenancy.

title: Termination notice and relocation assistance for no-fault just cause
requirement: For a no-fault just cause termination, the landlord must give written notice of the basis, the relocation assistance and the opportunity to re-rent, and pay two months of actual rent, or three for a senior or disabled tenant, or waive rent.
key_value: 2 months' rent (3 months if senior or disabled)
coverage_conditions: Tenants displaced by no-fault just cause termination under section 98.0704(b), regardless of income or length of tenancy; at-fault curable lease violations get notice and a chance to cure.
exemptions: No relocation assistance when a government agency or court finds the tenant at fault for the condition triggering the vacate order; assistance is credited against other assistance required by law.
penalty: Failure to strictly comply with section 98.0706 voids the termination notice; failure to pay relocation assistance brings liability of not less than three times the assistance plus actual damages, and wrongful recovery of possession brings at least three times actual economic damages plus attorney's fees.
quoted_span:
(A) The landlord shall provide a direct payment to the tenant.

(i) Unless section 98.0706(c)(1)(A)(ii) applies, the direct
payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to
two months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in
effect at the date of the notice.

(ii) If the tenant is a senior or disabled, the direct payment
to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to three
months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in effect
at the date of the notice.
interaction: Relocation assistance is credited against any other relocation assistance required by federal, state or local law.

title: Minimum screening criteria must be stated in re-rental offer to displaced tenant
requirement: When a landlord offers the unit again to a tenant displaced by a no-fault just cause termination, the written offer must state the minimum screening criteria used for the new tenancy.
coverage_conditions: A residential rental property offered for rent or lease within five years of the tenant's no-fault just cause eviction under sections 98.0704(b)(1), (3) or (4).

applicability.other: applies only if the property is re-offered within five years of the no-fault eviction

penalty: Failure to comply with any provision of the Division renders void any notice of termination.
quoted_span:
The landlord shall have the right to screen the tenant using industry accepted
methods and shall communicate the minimum screening criteria in the written
offer for the new tenancy.
